findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (line 160 of `UsernamePasswordForm.java`). There is no zero-argument overload in `UsernameForm` or any superclass, so `UsernameForm.java` fails to compile.

findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` requires `user != null`, breaking initial passkey login when no user is set yet
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both `authenticate(context)` (line 115) and `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) gate `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` on this method. On a normal initial login `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` always returns `false` and `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never called. As a result, WebAuthn conditional UI attributes and challenge are never added to the login form on initial login, completely breaking passwordless passkey login when the user is not yet identified. Even if `user != null`, it should also verify that the user actually has a passkey credential configured (`webauthnAuth.configuredFor(context.getSession(), context.getRealm(), user)`) rather than enabling passkey UI for any identified user.
